items.en: Black-soybean agar jelly with bean syrup and kinako
items.note: The signature. Hokkaido kurokuro black soybeans cooked deliberately firm, set with agar, poured with a syrup reduced from the bean cooking liquor (not brown sugar), kinako soy flour optional. Every documented component is plant-based and wheat-free — but this comes from visitors, not the shop, and the same tiny kitchen bakes wheat chiffon cakes daily. Ask before treating it as celiac-safe.

Four domestic beans — taisho kintoki, uzura, ootebou and Hokkaido azuki — slow-cooked without a pressure cooker, with a locally pounded grilled mochi. Mochi is glutinous rice, not wheat. Also written 四色福豆しるこ; reported at ¥750 in 2023 and ¥800 in 2025. Wheat handled in the same kitchen.

items.ja: 冷製　白玉ぜんざい
items.en: Chilled zenzai with shiratama and tofu ice cream
items.note: Hokkaido azuki with shiratama dumplings boiled to order and a spoon of the shop's own tofu ice cream. Shiratama is glutinous rice flour. Reported at ¥700 and ¥750.

Made with the same Kanazawa silken tofu (Ishikawa Enrei soybeans, Noto natural nigari) as the chiffons. Whether it is set with gelatin, agar or egg is not documented — ask, both for vegan and for celiac.

items.ja: とうふシフォン黒豆入り（1カット）
items.en: Tofu chiffon cake with black soybeans, by the slice
items.note: A visitor quotes the shop: selected HOKKAIDO WHEAT FLOUR with silken tofu folded through. The tofu is an addition, not a flour replacement — this is a wheat cake, and it is the reason to treat everything else here as shared-kitchen. Chiffon is normally egg-raised; confirm before calling it vegan.

items.en: Bean soup of the week, with a small rice
items.note: Created for customers who wanted something savoury; beans plus seasonal vegetables, changed every Friday, served with a small bowl of rice. The seasoning is undocumented — Japanese soups of this kind normally use soy sauce or miso and often a dashi. Ask on both counts.
¥50 off when taken with a sweet.
Whisked matcha. Usually comes with a small sweet — check what it is.
Leaf from the Kanazawa Japanese-and-Taiwanese tea specialist Chasha Mikoto. ¥450 hot, ¥550 iced.

items.ja: 自家製おとなのジンジャーエール
items.note: House-made ginger syrup with soda. A milder house ginger drink is also ¥600.

items.ja: 自家製あらごしりんごスカッシュ
items.note: House-made. A green-plum squash appears in season.
Dairy.

items.en: Meisei lunch (multi-dish brown-rice tray, drink included)
items.note: Reservation-only, and the whole shop is run by a Jodo-Shinshu priest who states plainly that no meat, fish, egg, dairy, MSG or additives are used — a third-party report confirms no fish is used even as dashi, which makes vegan unusually solid here. Gluten is the open question: the tray is built on multigrain brown rice and a 'grain burger', and the shop only says it uses traditionally-made seasonings, never that its soy sauce is wheat-free. Also caters for allergy and five-pungent-root exclusions if you ask in advance. NOTE: the published menu has not been updated since 2015, the shop's own domain is dead, and we found no 2026 evidence of trading — phone before you go.

items.section: 明制ランチの内容（ある日の献立） / Example lunch contents
items.note: Part of a documented lunch tray. Zakkoku multigrain mixes very often contain pressed barley or mochi-mugi — both gluten grains. Ask for plain brown rice with no zakkoku if you are celiac.

items.section: 明制ランチの内容（ある日の献立） / Example lunch contents
items.note: Part of a documented lunch tray, and the highest-risk item on it: grain and soy patties in Japan are commonly bound with wheat gluten, breadcrumbs or barley. Ask exactly which grains before eating it.

From ¥770; made to order. Same wheat questions as the sit-down trays.

items.section: 定番メニューではありません / Not a listed menu item
items.note: Recorded ONCE, in January 2015, as a special the cook made for a private party — it is not on the menu and you should not turn up expecting it. Described only as buckwheat flour and soy milk, with no statement that it is 100% buckwheat; Japanese soba flour is normally wheat-blended.

items.ja: ワンコインランチ「初めてのマクロ美ランチ」
items.romaji: wan koin ranchi hajimete no makurobi ranchi
items.en: Five-hundred-yen daily lunch (brown rice and multigrain, vegetable-centred), tea included
items.note: The whole operation is macrobiotic and describes itself as including vegan, so plant-based is safe ground. Gluten is not resolved: Kanazawa City's own food-barrier-free map tags this shop as having wheat-free menu items, yet the shop's flagship bread is organic WHOLEMEAL WHEAT — so 'wheat-free' clearly applies to some dishes and not others. Phone 090-4686-4124 and ask which. Comes with aged sannen-bancha or genmyocha.

items.ja: 玄米木の実パンセット
items.note: The set named on the shop's own verified listing. The bread it is built on is the shop's Heidi black bread, whose own product copy says ORGANIC WHOLEMEAL FLOUR — that is wheat. Do not order this one as a wheat-free option.
From the shop's own verified listing. Kombu is naturally wheat-free but is usually simmered with soy sauce — ask whether the seasoning is tamari.
From the shop's own verified listing. Brown-rice mochi and azuki are both wheat-free grains, which makes this the most promising sweet on the board — confirm nothing wheat-based is added.

items.en: Abekawa mochi (mochi with kinako and sugar)
items.note: Named in the shop's own cafe menu listing. Glutinous rice and roasted soy flour — both wheat-free grains in themselves.

items.ja: オーガニックぜんざい
items.note: Listed by the shop on the Kanazawa City food map. Sweet azuki soup.

items.ja: ブルーベリー・チェリーのスイーツ
items.note: Named on the shop's own cafe menu. No white sugar, no egg and no dairy anywhere in this kitchen; the base or crust is undocumented.

items.section: パン / Bread (retail and mail order)
items.note: The shop's own copy: made with ORGANIC WHOLEMEAL FLOUR and a generous quantity of nuts including kuko and other Chinese-medicine ingredients, no white sugar, no egg, no dairy. A green version with mugwort and spirulina or a beige version can be chosen. Vegan yes; gluten-free no — this is the wheat in the building.
The macrobiotic standard, caffeine-free, given free with the one-coin lunch. Plain roasted tea leaf and stem.
Roasted brown rice, so wheat-free in principle — but grain coffees sold in Japan are frequently cut with barley, so ask whether this one is rice only.

A yin-yang five-element blend of around 27 Japanese and Chinese medicinal herbs from Kurohime Wakan. Herbal blends of this size often include barley or hatomugi — ask for the ingredient list if you are celiac.

Retail kit from Genmai Kouso, also used in the shop's ¥500 hands-on miso-making session (with an aged-miso soup). Brown-rice koji miso is rice-based rather than barley-based, which matters if you are avoiding mugi miso — but confirm on the packet.
Sold over the counter in brown, half-milled and white. Plain rice is the honest survival food here: wheat-free, cheap, and you can cook it yourself.

items.ja: ナチュラルクッキング【ハイジの黒パン作り】

items.en: Natural cooking class: making Heidi's black bread
items.note: Per session, materials, food and teaching materials included, up to five people, advance booking required. Wholemeal wheat — worth knowing this is what gets handled in the same room.
